content: Dr. George A. Sheehan, born in 1918 in Brooklyn, New York, was a renowned cardiologist and an influential figure in the world of running. He gained widespread recognition for his books and writings on the sport, particularly his best-selling work, Running & Being: The Total Experience. During his college years, he excelled as a track athlete and later followed in his father’s footsteps to become a cardiologist. During World War II, he served as a physician in the United States Navy aboard the destroyer USS Daly (DD-519) in the South Pacific. He married Mary Jane Fleming, and together they raised twelve children. Despite battling prostate cancer later in life, he continued to write, with his final book, Going the Distance, being published shortly after his death in 1993. Dr. Sheehan was the eldest of 14 siblings. Although he was a track star at Manhattan College, he did not return to running until the age of 45, while living in Rumson, New Jersey. He began by running laps in his backyard, completing 26 loops to cover a mile. Eventually, he started running along the river road during his lunch breaks, often dressed in long underwear and a ski mask. Remarkably, five years after resuming running, he achieved a 4:47 mile, becoming the first 50-year-old in the world to run a mile in under five minutes. Dr. Sheehan began writing a weekly column for a local newspaper, a practice he maintained for 25 years. He also served as the medical editor for Runner’s World magazine, a role he took on after being introduced to Joe Henderson by Hal Higdon during the 1968 Olympics. Even after Runner’s World was acquired by Rodale Press, he continued to contribute to the publication. Over the course of his career, he authored eight books and delivered lectures around the globe. A devout Catholic, Dr. Sheehan co-founded Christian Brothers Academy in 1958, an all-boys preparatory school in Lincroft, New Jersey, near his home in Rumson. The school grew to become one of the most prestigious prep schools in the state. In 1986, he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. Despite his illness, he continued running until his physical condition no longer allowed it. During this time, his writing shifted focus from running to his experiences with illness and dying. His final book, Going the Distance, chronicled this journey and was published posthumously in 1993. Dr. Sheehan’s published works include the following: Dr. Sheehan on Running (1975) Dr. George Sheehan's Medical Advice for Runners (1978) Running & Being: The Total Experience (1978) This Running Life (1980) How to Feel Great Twenty Four Hours a Day (1983) Dr. Sheehan on Fitness (1983) Personal Best: The Foremost Philosopher of Fitness Shares Techniques and Tactics for Success and Self-Liberation (1989) George Sheehan on Running to Win: How to Achieve the Physical, Mental & Spiritual Victories of Running (1992) Going the Distance: One Man's Journey to the End of His Life (1996)
